claims.text: Two randomized placebo-controlled trials of 2 g twice in one day, started at first symptoms
claims.quote: Subjects were provided with 2 g of valacyclovir twice daily for 1 day (1-day treatment) ... and instructed to initiate treatment upon the first symptoms of a cold sore.

claims.text: Median episode 1.0 day shorter than placebo with 1-day treatment (about a day)
claims.quote: the median duration of the episode (primary endpoint) was reduced by 1.0 day (P = 0.001) with 1-day treatment

claims.text: Time to healing and time to end of pain or discomfort significantly shorter
claims.quote: The time to lesion healing and time to cessation of pain and/or discomfort were statistically significantly reduced with valacyclovir compared to placebo.

claims.text: Adverse events similar between valacyclovir and placebo
claims.quote: AEs were similar across treatment groups.

claims.text: Better absorption is what the researchers set out to test with a short high-dose course
claims.quote: Oral valacyclovir is better absorbed than oral acyclovir ... This provides the opportunity to explore whether high systemic acyclovir concentrations are effective in the treatment of cold sores

claims.text: Authors describe one-day valacyclovir as a convenient dosing alternative to topical therapies
claims.quote: The 1-day valacyclovir regimen offers patients a unique and convenient dosing alternative compared to available topical therapies.

claims.text: Valacyclovir and acyclovir were tested in separate placebo-controlled trials (with refs 4 and 7)
claims.quote: Two randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled studies were conducted.

claims.text: Cold sore dose 2 g twice in one day, 12 hours apart
claims.quote: The recommended dosage of VALTREX for treatment of cold sores is 2 grams twice daily for 1 day taken 12 hours apart.

claims.text: Start at the earliest symptom (tingling, itching, burning)
claims.quote: Therapy should be initiated at the earliest symptom of a cold sore (e.g., tingling, itching, or burning).

claims.text: Efficacy when started after a bump, blister or ulcer has not been established
claims.quote: The efficacy of VALTREX initiated after the development of clinical signs of a cold sore (e.g., papule, vesicle, or ulcer) has not been established.

claims.text: Do not exceed 1 day of treatment for cold sores
claims.quote: Cold sores (Herpes Labialis) Do not exceed 1 day of treatment.

claims.text: Renal dose for cold sores: two 1-g doses, two 500-mg doses, or a single 500-mg dose depending on kidney function
claims.quote: 30-49: Two 1-gram doses taken 12 hours apart; 10-29: Two 500-mg doses taken 12 hours apart; <10: 500-mg single dose

claims.text: Indicated for cold sores in adults and children 12 and older
claims.quote: VALTREX is indicated for the treatment of cold sores (herpes labialis) in pediatric patients aged greater than or equal to 12 years.

claims.text: Ester of acyclovir; nearly completely converted to acyclovir in gut and liver
claims.quote: the hydrochloride salt of the L-valyl ester of the antiviral drug acyclovir ... nearly completely converted to acyclovir and L-valine by first-pass intestinal and/or hepatic metabolism.

claims.text: Bioavailability of acyclovir after valacyclovir about 54 percent
claims.quote: The absolute bioavailability of acyclovir after administration of VALTREX is 54.5% ± 9.1%

claims.text: Activated by viral thymidine kinase; blocks DNA copying partly by chain termination
claims.quote: phosphorylated intracellularly by the viral encoded thymidine kinase (TK; pUL23) of HSV or VZV into acyclovir monophosphate ... incorporation and termination of the growing viral DNA chain

claims.text: Trial subjects started at earliest symptoms before any sign; episodes about 1 day shorter; 2-day regimen no added benefit
claims.quote: Subjects self-initiated therapy at the earliest symptoms and prior to any signs of a cold sore. The mean duration of cold sore episodes was about 1 day shorter in treated subjects as compared with placebo.

claims.text: Two-day course added no benefit over one-day
claims.quote: The 2-day regimen did not offer additional benefit over the 1-day regimen.

claims.text: Cold sore trial side effects headache 14% vs 10%, dizziness 2% vs 1%
claims.quote: VALTREX 2 grams twice daily (n = 609) or placebo (n = 609) for 1 day, respectively, included headache (14%, 10%) and dizziness (2%, 1%).

claims.text: Most common across uses: headache, nausea, abdominal pain
claims.quote: more commonly than in subjects treated with placebo are headache, nausea, and abdominal pain.

claims.text: Acute kidney failure reported in elderly, renal disease with higher-than-recommended doses, nephrotoxic drugs, inadequate hydration
claims.quote: Cases of acute renal failure have been reported in: Elderly patients ... Patients with underlying renal disease who received higher-than-recommended doses ... Patients receiving other nephrotoxic drugs. Patients without adequate hydration.

claims.text: Advise adequate hydration for all patients
claims.quote: Adequate hydration should be maintained for all patients.

claims.text: CNS effects such as agitation, confusion, hallucinations; older adults more likely
claims.quote: Central nervous system adverse reactions, including agitation, hallucinations, confusion, delirium, seizures ... Elderly patients are more likely to have central nervous system adverse reactions.

claims.text: Older adults more likely to need dose reduction and to have renal or CNS adverse events
claims.quote: Elderly patients are more likely to have reduced renal function and require dose reduction. Elderly patients are also more likely to have renal or CNS adverse events

claims.text: Contraindicated after clinically significant hypersensitivity (anaphylaxis, severe skin reaction) to valacyclovir, acyclovir or any component
claims.quote: contraindicated in patients who have had a demonstrated clinically significant hypersensitivity reaction [e.g., anaphylaxis, severe cutaneous adverse reactions (SCARs)] to valacyclovir, acyclovir, or any component of the formulation

claims.text: Efficacy and safety not established in immunocompromised (apart from one genital herpes use) or children under 12 with cold sores
claims.quote: The efficacy and safety of VALTREX have not been established in: Immunocompromised patients other than for the suppression of genital herpes in HIV-1-infected patients with a CD4+ cell count greater than or equal to 100 cells/mm3.

claims.text: Efficacy and safety not established in children under 12 with cold sores
claims.quote: The efficacy and safety of VALTREX have not been established in: ... Patients aged less than 12 years with cold sores (herpes labialis).

claims.text: Pregnancy: decades of data have not identified a drug-associated risk of major birth defects
claims.quote: Clinical data over several decades with valacyclovir and its metabolite, acyclovir, in pregnant women, have not identified a drug associated risk of major birth defects.

claims.text: Acyclovir passes into breast milk
claims.quote: its metabolite, acyclovir, is present in human milk following oral administration of valacyclovir.

claims.text: No clinically significant drug interactions known
claims.quote: No clinically significant drug-drug or drug-food interactions with VALTREX are known

claims.text: Can be taken with or without food
claims.quote: VALTREX may be given without regard to meals.

claims.text: Missed dose: take as soon as remembered; do not double
claims.quote: Instruct patients that if they miss a dose of VALTREX, to take it as soon as they remember. Advise patients not to double their next dose or take more than the prescribed dose.

claims.text: Label has no daily cold sore prevention regimen; its daily suppression doses are for genital herpes
claims.quote: The recommended dosage of VALTREX for chronic suppressive therapy of recurrent genital herpes is 1 gram once daily

claims.text: Prescription drug with an allergy contraindication and kidney-based dosing, so a clinician review precedes prescribing (review framing is editorial)
claims.quote: VALTREX is contraindicated in patients who have had a demonstrated clinically significant hypersensitivity reaction ... Elderly patients are more likely to have reduced renal function and require dose reduction.
